pinyin: yī kū èr nào sān shàng diào
literal: one · cry · two · make a scene · three · hang oneself

meaning.en: The full routine of an emotional blackmailer: first weep, then kick up a fuss, then threaten suicide to get one's way.
meaning.zh: 先哭，再闹，最后以寻死相威胁，用来逼人让步的一套手段。

equivalents: cry, scream and threaten the worst
pull out all the stops to get one's way

examples.zh: 她一哭二闹三上吊，非要家里给她买房。
examples.en: She wept, raged and threatened the worst until the family agreed to buy her a flat.

examples.zh: 别指望用一哭二闹三上吊来吓住我。
examples.en: Don't expect tears, tantrums and threats to scare me.

usage.en: Describes a stereotyped escalation, traditionally of a wife or woman in a quarrel; today it is used jokingly or disapprovingly of anyone who makes scenes to get what they want.
usage.zh: 指撒泼耍赖、步步升级的逼迫手段，旧时多形容妇女，今泛指无理取闹。

pinyin: yī bǎ yǎn lèi yī bǎ bí tì
literal: one · handful · tears · one · handful · snot

meaning.en: Crying messily and copiously, often while pouring out one's troubles.
meaning.zh: 哭得很厉害，眼泪鼻涕一齐流，常带着诉苦。

examples.zh: 她一把眼泪一把鼻涕地向我诉说委屈。
examples.en: She poured out her grievances to me in floods of tears.

examples.zh: 孩子摔了一跤，一把眼泪一把鼻涕地跑回家。
examples.en: The child fell over and ran home, sobbing his heart out.

usage.en: Used as an adverbial, usually with 地, or as a predicate: 哭得一把眼泪一把鼻涕. Can also hint that the crying is a bit theatrical.
usage.zh: 多作状语或补语。有时暗示哭得有点夸张。

pinyin: yī shì yī, èr shì èr
literal: one · is · one, two · is · two

meaning.en: To state things exactly as they are, without exaggeration or fudging; also, to be strict and not make exceptions.
meaning.zh: 是什么就说什么，不夸大不含糊；也指办事认真，不通融。

examples.zh: 账目要一是一，二是二，不能糊弄。
examples.en: The accounts must be exact, with no fudging.

examples.zh: 他做事一是一，二是二，从不讲情面。
examples.en: He does things strictly by the book and never makes allowances for friendship.

usage.en: Close in sense to 有一说一，有二说二, but more often applied to how a person handles matters, not only how they speak. Casual, usually predicate.
usage.zh: 与“有一说一，有二说二”相近，更常用来形容办事态度。多作谓语。

pinyin: shàng dāo shān, xià yóu guō
literal: climb · knife · mountain, descend · oil · wok

meaning.en: To be ready to face any danger or hardship, however terrible, for a cause or a person.
meaning.zh: 不怕任何艰难危险，什么苦都敢吃。

examples.zh: 为了救他，我上刀山，下油锅也愿意。
examples.en: To save him I would go through fire and water.

examples.zh: 只要你一句话，上刀山，下油锅我也去。
examples.en: Say the word, and I'll brave anything.

usage.en: The image is the 'mountain of knives' and 'pot of boiling oil' of Buddhist and folk visions of hell. Often follows 为了……, or is used with 敢 / 愿意.
usage.zh: 喻赴汤蹈火，意象来自民间传说中地狱的刀山油锅。常与“愿意”“敢”连用。

pinyin: liǎng ěr bù wén chuāng wài shì
literal: two · ears · not · hear · window · outside · matters

meaning.en: Paying no attention to what goes on outside one's own small world, whether through devotion to study or indifference.
meaning.zh: 不关心外界的事，一心只顾自己的事情，如埋头读书。

examples.zh: 备考期间，他两耳不闻窗外事，一心读书。
examples.en: While preparing for the exam he shut out the world and just studied.

examples.zh: 她两耳不闻窗外事，连最近的大新闻都不知道。
examples.en: She is so cut off that she hasn't heard even the biggest recent news.

usage.en: Often paired with 一心只读圣贤书 (fixing one's heart on the sages' books alone). Can be praise for focus or mild criticism of being out of touch.
usage.zh: 常与“一心只读圣贤书”连用。可夸专心，也可含贬义，指不关心世事。

antonyms: 读书不忘救国，救国不忘读书

pinyin: qián wú gǔ rén, hòu wú lái zhě
literal: before · no · ancients, after · no · those-to-come

meaning.en: Unmatched in the past and unlikely to be matched in the future; a one-off achievement.
meaning.zh: 以前没有人做到，以后也不会有人做到，形容成就空前绝后。

examples.zh: 他的成就前无古人，后无来者。
examples.en: His achievement is unprecedented and may never be repeated.

examples.zh: 这样的天才，真是前无古人，后无来者。
examples.en: A genius like this is truly without precedent or successor.

usage.en: Often recalls the line 前不见古人，后不见来者 in Chen Zi'ang's poem on Youzhou Terrace. Predicate or attributive; praise, sometimes hyperbolic.
usage.zh: 常让人联想到陈子昂《登幽州台歌》“前不见古人，后不见来者”。多作谓语、定语，带夸张的赞誉。

pinyin: shèng bù jiāo, bài bù něi
literal: win · not · be proud, lose · not · lose heart
natural: stay humble in victory, undaunted in defeat

meaning.en: Do not get arrogant when you win, and do not lose heart when you lose.
meaning.zh: 胜利了不骄傲，失败了不气馁。

equivalents: stay humble in victory and resilient in defeat
win without swagger, lose without despair

examples.zh: 做运动员要胜不骄，败不馁。
examples.en: An athlete must be neither swollen-headed in victory nor crushed in defeat.

examples.zh: 老师常教导我们：胜不骄，败不馁。
examples.en: Our teacher often tells us to stay modest when we win and hopeful when we lose.

usage.en: A maxim for sport, study and work, often appearing in speeches and school slogans. Neutral to formal in tone.
usage.zh: 常见于体育、学习、工作的格言与口号。

pinyin: bàn lù shā chū gè chéng yǎo jīn
literal: halfway · charge out · a · Cheng Yaojin

meaning.en: An unexpected person suddenly appears and upsets one's plans, usually a rival or troublemaker.
meaning.zh: 事情进行中突然冒出一个意想不到的人，打乱原来的计划。

examples.zh: 我们谈得好好的，半路杀出个程咬金，把合同抢走了。
examples.en: The deal was going well, then out of nowhere a rival turned up and snatched the contract.

examples.zh: 比赛中半路杀出个程咬金，夺走了冠军。
examples.en: An unexpected challenger came from nowhere and took the title.

usage.en: Cheng Yaojin was a Tang general; in the folk novels and storytelling about him he bursts in with an axe midway through the fight and changes the outcome. Also said 半路杀出的程咬金.
usage.zh: 程咬金是唐初名将，民间评书中他常半路杀出，扭转战局。

pinyin: zuì hòu yī gēn dào cǎo
literal: last · (measure word) · straw

meaning.en: The final small burden or incident that makes someone or something finally collapse after much accumulated pressure.
meaning.zh: 压垮人或事物的最后一点负担，前面已积累了很多压力。

equivalents: the straw that broke the camel's back

examples.zh: 这次失败成了压死骆驼的最后一根稻草。
examples.en: This failure was the last straw.

examples.zh: 加班一个月后，那条批评就是压死骆驼的最后一根稻草，他辞职了。
examples.en: After a month of overtime, that criticism was the last straw and he resigned.

usage.en: A loan from the English proverb about the straw that broke the camel's back, now thoroughly at home in Chinese. Usually 成为 / 是 + this phrase.
usage.zh: 借自英语谚语，现已通行于汉语。常说“成了压死骆驼的最后一根稻草”。

variants: 压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草
压死骆驼的最后一根稻草

pinyin: chuāi zhe míng bái zhuāng hú tu
literal: hold · understanding · pretend · muddled

meaning.en: To know perfectly well but pretend not to understand, usually to avoid a responsibility or a request.
meaning.zh: 心里明白，却假装不懂。

examples.zh: 他明明知道我们的意思，却揣着明白装糊涂。
examples.en: He knows exactly what we mean, yet plays dumb.

examples.zh: 别跟我揣着明白装糊涂，钱到底谁拿了？
examples.en: Don't play dumb with me; who took the money?

usage.en: Often said in an accusing tone. 揣 here means 'tuck in one's clothes', so the image is of carrying one's understanding hidden away. Compare 装聋作哑.
usage.zh: 多含指责。“揣”是藏在怀里，意思是把明白藏起来。

pinyin: jìng jiǔ bù chī chī fá jiǔ
literal: offered · wine · not · drink · drink · forfeit · wine
natural: refuse the friendly offer and get the hard way

meaning.en: To refuse a polite offer and so end up being forced to accept something worse.
meaning.zh: 不接受好言好语的请求，结果只能被迫接受更糟的待遇。

equivalents: refuse the carrot and get the stick
not take the easy way out

examples.zh: 你再不答应，就是敬酒不吃吃罚酒。
examples.en: If you still refuse, you'll be asking for the hard way.

examples.zh: 好好跟他说他不听，真是敬酒不吃吃罚酒。
examples.en: He wouldn't listen when spoken to nicely; he's choosing the hard way.

usage.en: At old drinking games the loser had to drink a penalty cup (罚酒). A threat or warning, often preceded by 别 or 不要.
usage.zh: 酒席上输了要罚酒；多用作威胁或警告，前面常加“别”。

pinyin: qǔ qí jīng huá, qù qí zāo pò
literal: take · its · essence, discard · its · dregs
natural: keep the best, drop the rest

meaning.en: Take what is good from something and throw away what is worthless or harmful.
meaning.zh: 吸收事物好的部分，抛弃不好的部分。

equivalents: keep the best and discard the rest
separate the wheat from the chaff

examples.zh: 对传统文化要取其精华，去其糟粕。
examples.en: Traditional culture should be treated by keeping its best and discarding the dross.

examples.zh: 学习外国经验，要取其精华，去其糟粕。
examples.en: Learn from foreign experience, but pick out the good and leave the bad.

usage.en: A stock formula of essays and official speeches, popularised in 20th-century debates about inheriting culture. Formal register.
usage.zh: 常见于议论文和官方文件，现代常用于谈对待传统文化和外来经验的态度。

pinyin: héng tiāo bí zi shù tiāo yǎn
literal: sideways · pick · nose · lengthways · pick · eyes

meaning.en: To nitpick and find fault in everything, from every angle.
meaning.zh: 故意从各方面挑剔、找毛病。

examples.zh: 婆婆对儿媳妇横挑鼻子竖挑眼。
examples.en: The mother-in-law finds fault with her daughter-in-law at every turn.

examples.zh: 他总是横挑鼻子竖挑眼，没一样东西满意。
examples.en: He keeps nitpicking and nothing satisfies him.

usage.en: The image is of criticising someone's nose and eyes whichever way they are turned. Typically predicate; 对……横挑鼻子竖挑眼.
usage.zh: 像对人家的鼻子眼睛左看右看地挑剔。多作谓语。

pinyin: zhǔ shú de yā zi fēi le
literal: cooked · duck · flew away

meaning.en: Something that seemed already won or secured is lost at the last moment.
meaning.zh: 眼看到手的东西又丢了，好事落空。

equivalents: see a sure thing slip away
lose what was in the bag

examples.zh: 订单被对手抢走，煮熟的鸭子飞了。
examples.en: The order was snatched by a rival; what we thought was in the bag has gone.

examples.zh: 别让到手的合同变成煮熟的鸭子飞了。
examples.en: Don't let the contract in your hands fly away like a cooked duck.

usage.en: Often with 眼看 or 竟然 to stress surprise. Colourful and slightly humorous; often used of deals and prizes.
usage.zh: 常与“眼看”“竟然”连用，带戏谑口吻，多用于生意、奖项。

pinyin: fù mǔ zhī mìng, méi shuò zhī yán
literal: parents · 's · command, matchmaker · 's · word

meaning.en: The traditional way of marrying: parents decide and a matchmaker arranges, with no free choice by the couple.
meaning.zh: 旧时婚姻由父母做主、媒人说合，当事人不能自己选择。

equivalents: by parental decree and matchmaker's word

examples.zh: 他们是父母之命，媒妁之言结的婚。
examples.en: They married by arrangement, as parents and matchmaker decided.

examples.zh: 她不愿接受父母之命，媒妁之言。
examples.en: She refused to accept a marriage arranged by her parents and a matchmaker.

usage.en: Refers to the traditional marriage system, which criticism of 'feudal' customs stressed. Often said in historical or critical contexts.
usage.zh: 指传统包办婚姻，现多用于谈历史或批判旧习俗。

story.en: Mencius condemns those who, 'without waiting for parents' orders and the matchmaker's word' (不待父母之命、媒妁之言), peep at each other through holes in the wall. The phrase later became the formula for arranged marriage.
story.zh: 《孟子·滕文公下》：“不待父母之命、媒妁之言，钻穴隙相窥，逾墙相从，则父母国人皆贱之。”

pinyin: bǎi huā qí fàng, bǎi jiā zhēng míng
literal: hundred · flowers · bloom together, hundred · schools · contend
natural: let a hundred flowers bloom and a hundred schools contend

meaning.en: Encouragement of free variety and open debate in art, science and thought.
meaning.zh: 提倡文艺和学术上自由发展、自由讨论。

equivalents: let a hundred flowers bloom and a hundred schools of thought contend

examples.zh: 我们要保持百花齐放，百家争鸣的学术氛围。
examples.en: We should keep an academic atmosphere in which a hundred flowers bloom and many schools contend.

examples.zh: 文艺创作应当百花齐放，百家争鸣。
examples.en: Literary and artistic creation should flourish in variety and open debate.

usage.en: A 1950s Chinese cultural policy slogan, taking its second half from the 'hundred schools' of the Warring States era. Formal; common in official language.
usage.zh: 20世纪50年代提出的文艺科学方针，“百家争鸣”指战国时期诸子争鸣。多用于正式场合。

origin.source: 毛泽东1956年提出的“双百”方针

story.en: In 1956 Mao Zedong put forward the policy that arts should 'let a hundred flowers bloom' and scholarship 'let a hundred schools contend', announced publicly in Lu Dingyi's report of 26 May 1956. The wording echoes the 'hundred schools' of the Warring States.
story.zh: 1956年毛泽东提出文艺“百花齐放”、学术“百家争鸣”的方针，同年5月陆定一作报告予以阐述；“百家争鸣”借用战国诸子之典。

pinyin: yǎn zhōng dīng, ròu zhōng cì
literal: eye · in · nail, flesh · in · thorn

meaning.en: A person one hates and wants rid of, who is always in the way.
meaning.zh: 最痛恨、最想除掉的人。

examples.zh: 他把竞争对手当成眼中钉，肉中刺。
examples.en: He regarded his rival as a thorn in his side.

examples.zh: 在这个小集团里，她是眼中钉，肉中刺。
examples.en: In this clique she is the one everyone wants out.

usage.en: Often shortened to 眼中钉 or 肉中刺, each used as a noun after 视为 / 当作.
usage.zh: 可单说“眼中钉”或“肉中刺”，常与“视为”“当作”连用。

pinyin: yǎn lǐ róng bù de shā zi
literal: eye · in · cannot · tolerate · sand

meaning.en: Unable to put up with any dishonesty, fault or injustice, however small.
meaning.zh: 一点不好的东西或不公正的事也不能容忍。

examples.zh: 他是个眼里容不得沙子的人。
examples.en: He is someone who cannot stand even the slightest wrong.

examples.zh: 会计要有眼里容不得沙子的原则。
examples.en: An accountant needs the principle of tolerating not a speck of error.

usage.en: Can be praise of integrity or a criticism of being too intolerant, depending on tone. Often as an attributive: 眼里容不得沙子的人.
usage.zh: 可夸人原则性强，也可指过于苛求。常作定语。

pinyin: yǎn guān liù lù, ěr tīng bā fāng
literal: eyes · watch · six · roads, ears · listen · eight · directions

meaning.en: To be highly alert and aware of everything going on around one.
meaning.zh: 形容人机警，对周围情况很留意。

equivalents: have eyes in the back of one's head
keep one's eyes and ears open

examples.zh: 做保安要眼观六路，耳听八方。
examples.en: A security guard has to keep eyes and ears open on all sides.

examples.zh: 他眼观六路，耳听八方，什么都瞒不过他。
examples.en: Alert to everything, nothing escapes him.

usage.en: Said of drivers, guards, salesmen, reporters, and anyone who has to stay sharp. Also written without the comma.
usage.zh: 常用来形容司机、保安、记者等需警觉的人，也有不加逗号的写法。

pinyin: zhēng zhe yǎn jing shuō xiā huà
literal: open · eyes · tell · blind · talk

meaning.en: To tell obvious lies in a straight-faced manner, even when the truth is plain for all to see.
meaning.zh: 明明知道事实，却当面说谎。

examples.zh: 证据都在这儿，你还睁着眼睛说瞎话！
examples.en: The evidence is right here, and you're still lying through your teeth!

examples.zh: 他睁着眼睛说瞎话，把责任全推给别人。
examples.en: He lied barefacedly and pushed all the blame on to others.

usage.en: Often an accusation. 瞎话 means a groundless lie; the image is of lying with one's eyes open.
usage.zh: 多含指责。“瞎话”指没有根据的假话。

text: 端起碗吃肉，放下筷子骂娘
pinyin: duān qǐ wǎn chī ròu, fàng xià kuài zi mà niáng
literal: pick up · bowl · eat · meat, put down · chopsticks · curse · mother

meaning.en: To enjoy benefits from someone or something while cursing and criticising it.
meaning.zh: 享受着好处，却对给自己好处的人或事物破口大骂。

equivalents: bite the hand that feeds one
enjoy the benefits and then complain

examples.zh: 有些人端起碗吃肉，放下筷子骂娘，真让人寒心。
examples.en: Some people eat the meat and then curse the cook, which is disheartening.

examples.zh: 他靠公司吃饭，却整天端起碗吃肉，放下筷子骂娘。
examples.en: He lives off the company yet slags it off all day.

usage.en: A vivid pair of clauses; the cursing uses 骂娘 ('swear at someone's mother'). Often said of ingratitude.
usage.zh: 两句对照鲜明；“骂娘”是粗口骂人。多指忘恩负义。

pinyin: lǎo po hái zi rè kàng tóu
literal: wife · children · warm · heated brick bed

meaning.en: A simple, contented life with wife, child and a warm bed; modest happiness at home.
meaning.zh: 有老婆孩子，有热炕头，形容安于家庭小日子的朴素生活。

equivalents: wife, kids and a warm hearth

examples.zh: 他的理想不过是老婆孩子热炕头。
examples.en: His ideal is no more than a wife, kids and a warm bed.

examples.zh: 农村人最满足的是老婆孩子热炕头。
examples.en: What country folk are most content with is a wife, kids and a warm kang.

usage.en: Often self-deprecating or slightly mocking of modest ambition. 炕 is the heated brick bed in northern homes.
usage.zh: 常带自嘲或揶揄，意思是胸无大志，只图安稳。“炕”是北方取暖的砖床。

pinyin: cōng míng yī shì, hú tu yī shí
literal: clever · all one's life, muddled · for a moment
natural: clever for a lifetime, foolish for a moment

meaning.en: Even a very clever person can make a stupid mistake once.
meaning.zh: 再聪明的人也会有一时犯糊涂的时候。

equivalents: clever all his life, a fool for a moment

examples.zh: 他聪明一世，糊涂一时，竟然上了骗子的当。
examples.en: Clever all his life, he was fooled for a moment by a conman.

examples.zh: 我真是聪明一世，糊涂一时，把钥匙锁在车里了。
examples.en: I was clever all my life and stupid for a moment: I locked my keys in the car.

usage.en: A sympathetic or teasing comment after a slip. Usually 真是…, or the second half is added as a punchline after someone's mistake.
usage.zh: 常用于别人或自己出错之后的感叹或打趣。
